01 — ABOUT ME

A practical mindset.
A connected
perspective.

I’m interested in what data can tell us — and what we can build with it.

My path into data science builds on hands-on experience in networks and systems. Supporting college campuses taught me to troubleshoot carefully, understand real needs, and make technology useful for the people behind it.

Through my M.S. in Data Science at Carolina University and my capstone work, I’ve been exploring Python, natural language processing, and content-based recommendation systems. My job recommendation project brings those interests together: turning résumé text and job descriptions into explainable matches.

I also bring a practical foundation in multi-vendor networks, Linux administration, cloud services, and security — alongside experience mentoring interns and supporting teams.

EXPLAINABLE BY DESIGN01

DATA SCIENCE CAPSTONE · 2026

AI-Based Job
Recommendation System

A content-based recommender that compares résumé text with job postings, ranks relevant roles, and explains the terms and skills behind each match.

I built a Python workflow for text cleaning, TF-IDF feature extraction, and cosine-similarity ranking, with a Streamlit interface for exploring recommendations and potential skill gaps.

  • Python
  • NLP
  • scikit-learn
  • pandas
  • Streamlit
Try the working app Read the case study
Download the Streamlit project
Inside the project
THE PROBLEM

Less searching. More context.

Job descriptions and résumés use varied language. The project explores how text-based similarity can surface relevant roles and make the reasons for a recommendation visible.

THE APPROACH

From raw text to ranked roles.

Clean and normalize the text, represent unigrams and bigrams with TF-IDF, then rank postings by cosine similarity. Shared terms, matched skills, and missing skills help explain each result.

THE EXPERIENCE

A workflow people can explore.

The Streamlit app accepts PDF, DOCX, or TXT résumés, works with imported job data or supported job APIs, and offers filters, charts, and downloadable recommendation results.

THE EVALUATION

Measure ranking quality.

The evaluation workflow supports human relevance ratings and calculates Precision@5, nDCG@10, and mean reciprocal rank. Similarity scores describe text alignment, rather than the likelihood of being hired.

02 / IoT

FINAL-YEAR PROJECT · 2020–2021

Patient Health
Monitoring System

Connecting physical sensors with a digital interface. My project explored Arduino-based vital-signal monitoring, LCD readings, and a web dashboard design.

  • Arduino Mega
  • Sensors
  • Interface design
Explore the project
From sensor to screen.

I connected heart-rate, ECG, and gyroscopic sensors to an Arduino Mega and displayed readings on an LCD. I also developed the circuit design and wireframes for the dashboard, login, and signup screens.

Building in stages.

The interim report documents sensor setup and interface development. GSM alerts, GPS, and full web integration formed part of the planned next stages. This was an academic development project; clinical accuracy was not established.

Work: circuit design · sensor setup · UI wireframes

Security Incident
Investigation

  • Kali Linux

Explore the project
Follow the evidence.

I documented a simulated compromise using Metasploit, then examined the suspicious email, downloaded files, browser activity, and background process involved in the scenario.

Turn findings into safeguards.

The report connects the investigation to practical recommendations around suspicious attachments, security awareness, and keeping endpoint and firewall protections enabled.

Work: investigation report · evidence screenshots · recommendations
